_comment: Human-approval ledger for the three mandatory pipeline gates (see ADR 0008, ADR 0013). Gate 1 = dramaturgy approved before visual prompts begin. Gate 1R = reference images approved before Phase-2 scene prompts begin (two-phase episodes, EP10 onward). Gate 2 = motion script approved before video generation begins. This is an HONEST record: it certifies that a human approved a specific artifact on a date. The sha256 pins WHICH bytes were approved so post-approval drift is visible; it CANNOT verify that the taste behind the approval was sound. pipeline_integrity.py consumes this file: artifacts beyond a gate with no record here = FAIL; a sha256 that no longer matches disk = WARN (post-approval em-dash cleanups are legitimate, the WARN just makes them visible).

gates.1: Dramaturgy approval - human sign-off before visual prompts begin
gates.1R: References approval - human sign-off on reference images before Phase-2 scene prompts begin (two-phase episodes, EP10 onward, ADR-0013)
gates.2: Motion script approval - human sign-off before video generation begins

references approved at the Phase-1 reference gate (two-phase run, ADR-0013): six environment references A-F generated and human-approved. The Step-0 decomposition split the dawn town into three camera-spaces - REF D residential lane (S03-S08), REF E market edge (S11-S12), REF F far-edge descent (S19-S22) - so REF E and REF F were authored and generated fresh (the single-pass draft under-mapped the town onto one ref); REF A-D carried forward unchanged, their approved images frozen in raw/. Artifact-pinned to the frozen Phase-1 v01; Phase 2 authors every scene against these approved reference pixels. Honest limit: 1R attests a human approved the references; the ref IMAGES live in gitignored raw/ and are not machine-verifiable (same posture as gates 1 and 2).
